title: Derivative of sinc(x) at x=0 returns NaN, should be 0

labels.name: module: numerical-stability
labels.description: Problems related to numerical stability of operations

labels.name: module: autograd
labels.description: Related to torch.autograd, and the autograd engine in general

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
## 🐛 Bug

Pytorch computes the derivative of `torch.sinc(x)` at `x=0` to be NaN. Usually the derivative of `sinc` is considered 0 at `x=0`. See e.g. [wolfram alpha](https://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=derivative+of+sinc%28x%29), or it can be found via [L'Hôpital's rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%27Hôpital%27s_rule).

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

```python
>>> import torch
>>> x = torch.Tensor([0])
>>> x.requires_grad = True
>>> y = torch.sinc(x)
>>> y.backward()
>>> print(x.grad)
tensor([nan])
```

## Expected behavior

I would expect the derivative to be computed as 0:

```python
>>> import torch
>>> x = torch.Tensor([0])
>>> x.requires_grad = True
>>> y = torch.sinc(x)
>>> y.backward()
>>> print(x.grad)
tensor([0.])
```

## Why?

The `sinc` function is critical for creating butterworth filters used heavily in digital signal processing. My network builds filters based on predicted passbands, but it fails to train because the derivative comes out as NaN.
